history.dynasty: Chola king Rajarajan-II; later additions by Pandyas and Vijayanagaras
history.summary: East-facing Shiva temple at Perumanam village with sanctum, antarala and ardha mandapam. Inscriptions record it was built in brick and mortar by Chola king Rajarajan-II (c. 1156 CE), with later contributions from the Pandyas and Vijayanagaras; the walls and adhistanam bear inscriptions of Kulothunga-III (1178-1218 CE), Rajaraja-III (1216-1257 CE) and Jatavarma Pandiyan (1251-1271 CE), mostly recording land donations for regular poojas. The place, Perumpunam in Sangam to Vijayanagara literature, is attested since the Sangam Age, and the village once had Jain and Hindu temples of which this is one of the survivors. IDENTITY FLAG: the CSV row is only 'Kailasanathar Temple, Thiruvannamalai' - there is no single canonical Kailasanathar Temple in Thiruvannamalai town; other Kailasanathar temples exist in the district (Kovilur, Narthampoondi - one of the seven Sapthakailasas on the Cheyyar river - and a geocoded 'Arulmighu Periyanayagi Samedha Kailasanathar Thirukovil' at 12.41205, 79.06719 north of the town). This record is mapped to the Perumanam temple, the only one with detailed published Thiruvannamalai-district documentation; confirm against the master CSV's intent. TOWN NOTE: actual location is Perumanam village; the CSV town Thiruvannamalai is the nearest city (~23 km). COORD FLAG: coordinates are Perumanam village centre, approximate - exact temple coordinates unverified. HOURS FLAG: no fixed opening hours are published; confirm with the local gurukkal before visiting. MEDIA NOTE: no verified image obtainable after a genuine search (blogger image hosts of the published temple photos stalled on fetch).
